 Advertisement Thanksgiving travel warning for Marylanders as AAA flags worst traffic times on Nov. 24-30
 Advertisement Updated: 12:59 PM EST Nov 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Greg Ng Digital Content Manager Thanksgiving travel warning for Marylanders as AAA flags worst traffic times on Nov. 24-30
 Updated: 12:59 PM EST Nov 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Greg Ng Digital Content Manager BALTIMORE — Some Marylanders traveling during Thanksgiving week will join more than 81.5 million Americans who are expected to travel for the holiday, according to AAA.
 Video above: Air travel expected to recover after last week's ground stop ( Story ) 
 Advertisement AAA Club Alliance said the number of Americans traveling this year is relatively unchanged from last year despite higher costs that have ended three years of record growth. While slightly fewer people are flying or taking road trips, more travelers are choosing cruises, buses and trains.
 Check our LIVE traffic map and cameras in the WBAL-TV 11 News app 
 "Apart from the pandemic years, this is the first time in eight years that Thanksgiving travel growth has held steady. Americans aren't staying home this Thanksgiving, but they're feeling the impact of higher travel costs," AAA Club Alliance spokeswoman Ragina Ali said in a statement.
 CAR TRAVEL : AAA projects 72.9 million people to travel by car for Thanksgiving, a slight drop from last year due in part to this season's record-high gas prices. The previous highest Thanksgiving record at the pump was in 2022 at $3.58.
 CAR RENTALS : Based on advance bookings, AAA cited Hertz data as showing Orlando, Florida; Phoenix, Arizona; Las Vegas, Nevada; Atlanta, Georgia; and Denver, Colorado, as the cities with the highest demand for rental cars, most of which are expected to be picked up on Nov. 24-25.
 AIR TRAVEL : AAA projects 5.96 million travelers will take domestic flights for Thanksgiving, a 0.2% decrease from last year. Air travelers make up more than 7% of the share of holiday travelers, like they did over Thanksgiving 2025.
 AAA said the main difference this year is how much more travelers are paying. According to AAA data, which is based on what travelers paid when they booked their Thanksgiving trips, round-trip domestic flights are 17% more expensive, averaging $800 per ticket.
 OTHER TRAVEL MODES : In a category that's growing, AAA projects 2.6 million Americans will take buses, trains and cruises — a 4.1% increase from last year.
 "Even with growth flattening, travelers should plan for busy roads and packed airports," Ali said. "Roughly one in four Americans will be on the move this Thanksgiving."
 Driving during Thanksgiving
 INRIX projects heavy holiday traffic on Nov. 24-25, as well as Nov. 28-30 for the return trip home.
 Here's when INRIX projects the best and worst times to travel by car will be.
 Worst times to travel
 Tuesday, Nov. 24: 2-8 p.m.
 Wednesday, Nov. 25: Noon-7 p.m.
 Thursday, Nov. 26: Minimal traffic expected
 Friday, Nov. 27: 1-7 p.m.
 Saturday, Nov. 28: Noon-9 p.m.
 Sunday, Nov. 29: Noon-8 p.m.
 Monday, Nov. 30: 2-7 p.m.
 Best times to travel
 Tuesday, Nov. 24: Before 1 p.m.
 Wednesday, Nov. 25: Before noon
 Friday, Nov. 27: Before noon
 Saturday, Nov. 28: Before 11 a.m.
 Sunday, Nov. 29: Before 11 a.m.
 Monday, Nov. 30: Before 1 p.m.
 Peak congestion by metro area
 Washington, D.C. to Baltimore
 Peak congestion on the Baltimore-Washington Parkway on Nov. 24 around 4:30 p.m. with an estimated travel time of 1 hour and 53 minutes, a 132% increase compared to typical travel times.
 Philadelphia to the Poconos
 Peak congestion on northbound Interstate 476 on Nov. 24 around 4:30 p.m. with an estimated travel time of 4 hours and 15 minutes, a 58% increase compared to typical travel times.
 New York to the Hamptons
 Peak congestion on the eastbound Long Island Expressway on Nov. 24 around 4:30 p.m. with an estimated travel time of 4 hours and 15 minutes, a 138% increase compared to typical travel times.
 AAA's top Thanksgiving weekend destinations
 Florida tops the list of domestic destinations for AAA members who booked their trips through AAA Travel, mainly for the theme parks and cruise vacations.
 Detroit and Dallas are also in the top 10 as the cities are hosting Thanksgiving Day football games.
